messages.text: Take {gift_item}. Good gear should travel, not gather dust.
Here, {gift_item}. It has more use with you than sitting by my cauldron.
Good. {gift_item} sat well with {tested_villager}, like softened leather.
Then the fit was comfortable. {tested_villager} liked {gift_item}.
Too stiff for them, then. For {gift_subject}, try {alternative_gift}.
{gift_item} rubbed wrong? Bring {alternative_gift}; better fit, less complaint.
That advice chafed. {alternative_gift} should sit easier.
You wore bad advice too long. Trade it for {alternative_gift}.

openings.text: Mind the tannery. What do you need?

closings.text: Back to curing leather without wasting hide, then.

lines.text: Bad stitching in the rain tells on itself quickly.
Gear that lasts is mostly patience made visible.
A split seam can ruin a journey faster than a bad map.
Mind the tannery. The smell is honest, at least.
A stitch done poorly waits for the worst time to confess.
Good leather is patience you can wear.
I once made boots that outlasted three owners and four bad roads.
Leather jokes need a thick skin. I keep saying that until someone laughs.
That sentence split like cheap stitching.
Rain tells the truth about gear faster than any seller will.
A pack should carry weight without reminding you every step.
My apron has seen enough mistakes to deserve its own corner by the fire.
Do not mock work that lasts longer than your manners.

pacify.text: Fine. I will stitch this shut for now.
That is not enough to mend it. Bring {emerald_cost} {emeralds}.
No. This split runs too deep for emeralds.
